races.name: Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Alta Regina
runners_data.note: Showed raw ability winning over 5f on Good but steps up sharply in class and numbers here; her natural front-running tendency is likely to be frustrated by Big Negotiator and Bint Archange, and she will be forced to race in a more restrained position than suits her.|
runners_data.comment: Alta Regina won three starts back and has run over today's trip, returning after 26 days in what looks a sound preparation; the worry is that sixth and seventh in her two most recent outings suggest she needs to rediscover that winning form quickly from stall eight off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Angels Passing
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good on most recent start and is a confirmed front-runner, but a 77-day absence and the presence of two equally aggressive pace horses make securing a clean lead unlikely; Kevin Stott will have to fight hard early just to remain prominent.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well toward the foot of the field on our figures, Angels Passing also returns after 77 days off, making her hard to fancy at the weights despite a winning effort last time out and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: Top-rated lead horse in the field at OR 102, wears a visor, and boasts six runs all on Good ground including 6f experience — the most credible of the three front-runners and capable of controlling this if rivals kick wide early.|
runners_data.comment: Big Negotiator won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but her two runs before that brought a fourth and an unplaced effort, and her rating of 98 ranks her ninth of nineteen here, suggesting she faces a stiff ask against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partnership immediately elevates her claims; two wins on Good but has shown a tendency to get outpaced over 5f, and this longer 6f test on fast ground with Moore able to dictate from the front suits her profile well.|
runners_data.comment: Bint Archange won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, but a ninth last time out is hard to overlook, and 128 lb from stall 9 adds to the challenge for a filly ranked in the lower half of this field.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Consistent if not yet a winner on Good ground this season, and David Egan's positive riding style could suit a prominent pitch here; the concern is that a 22-day turnaround into a deep 19-runner Group 2 field is a significant test of readiness.|
runners_data.comment: Crownbreaker won two starts back but has been unplaced on her most recent outing, and at 128 lb she faces a stiff ask; she has run over today's trip and going, and drawing stall three gives her a neutral position heading into this competitive heat.

runners_data.name: Crystal Queen
runners_data.note: The only genuinely confirmed hold-up runner in the race, and Connor Beasley will be hoping the pace war hands her a chance to close late; 64 days off the track is the main query, but her 5f win and place on Good ground are solid credentials.|
runners_data.comment: Crystal Queen won two starts back and was second three starts back, but comes into this unplaced last time out and a 64-day absence makes fitness the key question; she has run over today's trip and the 128 lb burden is no help from stall 19.

runners_data.name: Desert Sands
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 75 and has not shown the form to trouble these; naturally prominent but mapped to the rear given the field's surplus of pace, meaning she is likely to race in an unfamiliar rearward position entirely out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Desert Sands faces a stiff ask here, though a third last time out at least hints at some residual form, and she has run over today's trip before, returning on a quick nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a single 5f win on Good and a very high OR 120 that may reflect potential rather than proven achievement; Geoff Oldroyd's operation rarely lands at this level and her unknown style adds uncertainty to how she handles this complex race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of a 19-runner field on our figures, In The Black faces a stiff task despite winning last time out; she has run over today's trip before, but 57 days off the track and a speed rating of just 47 make her hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Jolivette
runners_data.note: William Buick is a significant booking for Andrew Balding's filly who won over 6f Good at Newmarket, but her natural prominence means she will be squeezed out of position by the more committed pace horses — she needs to find a cleaner run than the map suggests she'll get.|
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has disappointed since, finishing ninth and fifth in her last two outings; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 41 days off may have freshened her up, though she faces a competitive field from stall 14 off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Libertango
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly has won her last two starts over 6f on Good ground and arrives in the best recent form of the genuine prominent contenders; Billy Loughnane's ability to place her just behind the pace battle without getting involved in the lead duel is the crucial tactical question.|
runners_data.comment: Libertango arrives here in sharp form, a winner in two of her last three starts with a second thrown in, and she has run over today's trip before. Carrying 128 lb from stall 15, a 41-day break is the only minor query on an otherwise compelling profile.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.note: Aidan's Lyons filly arrives on the back of back-to-back 6f Good wins and only 17 days ago, meaning she is at peak fitness; Colin Keane's tactical intelligence over this exact trip on Good ground makes her one of the most compelling profiles in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the top of this field on our figures, Livenka faces a stiff ask from stall 18 carrying 128 lb, though she arrives in fair heart having won two of her last four starts, and she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Love A Giggle
runners_data.note: Won twice earlier in the season but has finished fourth on her most recent run and is a natural front-runner who will be shuffled into a midfield berth she is not bred or trained to occupy; the style mismatch is a genuine concern at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Boasting two wins in her last four starts, Love A Giggle arrives on a sound fitness margin of 19 days, has run over today's trip and going, and draws stall two carrying 128 lb; a fourth last time out and an unplaced effort two starts back temper enthusiasm, though our rating of 100 suggests residual ability.

runners_data.name: Miss Kodi
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft and is unproven on Good ground, which is the main query; Clive Cox trains her well fresh and Rossa Ryan is a smart booking, but her true prominent style will be forced back into midfield by the traffic, limiting her chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out but that was two starts back — she steps back up having finished fifth most recently, which tempers confidence; has run over today's trip and a rating of 101 gives her claims, though she faces a competitive 19-runner field from stall seven carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's second runner holds strong form with back-to-back wins including over 6f Good at Newmarket; Oisin Murphy partners her and can be trusted to find a position tracking the hot pace before delivering a challenge, making her a natural beneficiary of the pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Moonrise arrives in fine nick, a winner last time out and two wins in her last three starts, and she has run over today's trip before; 128 lb and stall 16 are the questions she must answer.

runners_data.name: Ruby Moon
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 6f Good and returns after 41 days; Richard Fahey's yard is in strong form (7 from 34 over 14 days) and Oisin Orr knows this horse, but she steps into Group 2 company with limited experience and needs plenty to go right.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out after winning the start before, though she has been off the track for 41 days and faces a field of 19 from stall 12 carrying 128 lb; she has run over today's trip before, and a rating of 96 gives her a fighting chance of mixing it mid-division.

runners_data.name: Sexy Chick
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground earlier this season but ran only six days ago and finished eighth most recently — the quick back-up is a concern; her natural prominence will be squeezed back and the combination of recent exertion and a deeper position works against her.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Sexy Chick faces a stiff ask, and her eighth last time out — just six days ago — does little to inspire confidence, though she has winning form two starts back and has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's filly won over 5f Good and finished second on her most recent start; Tom Marquand is a capable partner but stepping up to 6f in a 19-runner Group 2 is a significant ask, and her form at this level has not yet been truly tested.|
runners_data.comment: Shimmering Sun arrives on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, and a winner one start back from that seventh, giving her a lively recent profile; the 29-day break and experience over today's trip and going are both in her favour, though that seventh remains the one blot to forgive.

runners_data.name: Star Of State
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR 120 alongside In The Black, and Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite booking who won the Derby and has serious big-field experience; her two-run 6f Good profile is exactly right and she must be respected as the class act.|
runners_data.comment: Star Of State won last time out and was second two starts back, so recent form reads well enough, but ranked 14 of 19 on our figures she faces a stiff ask against this field despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Wild Blossom
runners_data.note: K R Burke's second runner has won two of three starts including over 5f Good and James Doyle takes over in the saddle — a positive change; her prominent style should allow her to track pace comfortably and she is a live chance if the field fans wide.|
runners_data.comment: Wild Blossom arrives on the back of a win last time out, and was a winner three starts back too, with only an unplaced run in between; she has distance and going experience to call on, though 128 lb is the one weight to respect.

races.paceDynamic: Big Negotiator, Bint Archange, and Angels Passing are all confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner field, guaranteeing a fierce early duel for the lead on York's straight six-furlong track, with an honest, relentless gallop from the outset on Good ground. That speed duel will compress the pack early, create significant traffic congestion two to three furlongs out as eight runners chase a prominent position, and the sustained pace will ruthlessly expose any lack of stamina or tactical weakness. With the pace likely to burn itself out, horses who can travel smoothly in the first two or three positions without being trapped in the melee — particularly those with class and proven 6f form on Good ground — are best placed to benefit as the front-runners tire in the final furlong. Closers tracking the hot pace from a genuine midfield position are the profile to favour here, provided they find a clean passage through the inevitable traffic; true hold-up horses rate more vulnerable given the field is actually short of genuine hold-up types, and several horses mapped to the rear are naturally prominent-running animals racing out of role. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than the track can accommodate — Big Negotiator and Bint Archange are most likely to physically secure the lead, with Angels Passing forced to slot just behind them, and runners like Jolivette, Miss Kodi, Alta Regina, Love A Giggle, and Sexy Chick will find themselves wider or deeper than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Big Negotiator, Bint Archange, and Angels Passing burns furiously enough to leave all three flattening inside the final furlong, allowing horses racing smoothly just off the pace to pick them off.
scenarios.body: Libertango, Livenka, Star Of State, and Moonrise — all with strong 6f Good-ground form and proven ability to track pace before quickening — will be perfectly positioned to accelerate as the leaders wilt, rewarding those whose jockeys kept a clean line through the traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator — the highest-rated of the three front-runners and proven over similar conditions — breaks sharply and forces Bint Archange and Angels Passing into a chase rather than a true duel, allowing him to control tempo and conserve enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: With a visor fitted and the most experienced Good-ground profile in the field (six runs, six on Good), Big Negotiator could dictate terms from a controlled position, with the pace honest enough to test rivals but not self-destructive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Wide Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion two furlongs out creates a logjam in the main body of the field, and a runner drawn wide or willing to come widest of all finds a clear unobstructed run to the line.
scenarios.body: Livenka, Wild Blossom, or Shimmering Sun — genuine prominent types with the quality to sustain a run if they find daylight — could emerge from a muddled finish, particularly if ridden to bypass the scrimmage along the far rail.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that true hold-up horses — or those mapped to the rear — find a gap opening late and fly home past the flattening pack.
scenarios.body: Crystal Queen is the only genuine hold-up type by style in this field, and while the scenario is possible, the horses shown further back (Desert Sands, In The Black) are not naturally suited to being ridden cold, making a clean late swoop harder to execute reliably.

watchPoints.text: Big Negotiator, Bint Archange, and Angels Passing — watch for an aggressive three-way pace battle from the outset that could produce a chaotic, compressed pack through the first two furlongs, sharply increasing collision risk near the stands rail.

Traffic danger two furlongs out is severe with eight runners targeting prominent positions in a straight-track 19-runner field — watch for Jolivette, Miss Kodi, Love A Giggle, and Alta Regina to be caught wide or checked as the bunched field tries to accelerate simultaneously.

Star Of State — Ryan Moore switches to Bint Archange, freeing Dylan Browne McMonagle for Joseph O'Brien's filly; watch whether the stable confidence behind the booking translates into a bold front-of-pack ride or a more patient campaign in a field this competitive.

In The Black — OR 120 with a single 5f win is an unusual profile for a Group 2 sprint field; watch whether she handles the step up to 6f and the significant increase in company, as her lightly raced tag means her true ceiling is genuinely unknown.

Angels Passing — watch for any signs of freshness or difficulty getting into stride after 77 days off, as a slow break from a confirmed front-runner in this pace-heavy field could see her immediately buried and unable to influence the race shape at all.

races.name: Harry's Half Million By Goffs (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tokaido
runners_data.note: Four wins from five starts including three consecutive on good ground, all over five or six furlongs; Amy Murphy's top-rated runner (OR 120) is versatile enough to track the pace and quicken, making this strong-gallop scenario a potential sweet spot.
runners_data.comment: Tokaido arrives in fine nick after four wins in his last five starts, most recently a winner 32 days ago, and with stall four drawn and 135 lb to carry, this unexposed gelding looks open to further improvement.

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner with a solid nine-from-ten record on similar going; naturally wants to race prominently but with so many confirmed pace horses in this field, Kevin Stott's withdrawn leaves Sean Kirrane managing a horse unlikely to secure its preferred position — temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Furturra has winning form in recent starts, scoring three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going; but a fourth last time out after 40 days off raises a fitness query, and 133 lb from stall 12 adds to the task.

runners_data.name: Mind Those Steps
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who won over this course and distance last time on good ground; blinkers fitted, David Allan rides, and the big field gives him a path if the pace burns through — but the 0/10 finishing record in poor recent form (3-1-0 in career, last seen finishing 11th at Sandown) is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the field on our figures, Mind Those Steps is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and a third three starts back; he has experience of today's distance and going, but an unplaced effort last time out makes him difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly is a true hold-up type who won on good ground over five furlongs twice before finishing fourth over this trip; Billy Loughnane takes over in a field of 22 where a truly strong pace could genuinely produce a late runway for her.
runners_data.comment: Where Love Lives won back-to-back races earlier in his recent form and returns on a quick enough turnaround at 21 days, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour; the worry is that his last two runs have been an unplaced effort and a fourth.

runners_data.name: The Bookkeeper
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes juvenile with modest good-ground form (0W from four starts on similar surfaces); races prominently but has shown a tendency to over-race and fade, and stepping up in class here is a stiff ask with OR 82.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out keeps The Bookkeeper in the mix, though a fourth two starts back tempers expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall 19, and a winner three starts back suggests the ability is there when things click.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on A P O'Brien's flagbearer is three-from-five on good ground, has won over this exact trip and course conditions twice, leads from the front, and sits in the highest OR band for front-runners — the single most dangerous pace setter in the field.
runners_data.comment: Sun Goddess has been in terrific nick, winning two on the spin and recording three wins in her last five starts, and she has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 130 lb from stall 17 is the one question, but her form makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's juvenile won over five furlongs on good ground last time and naturally wants to be prominent; however, the volume of pace in this field means Kevin Stott will struggle to hold that position, the horse's chance is structurally compromised by the race shape before it even runs.
runners_data.comment: Battle Fever won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform at 128 lb from stall 5, but a trainer firing at just 5% in the last fortnight is a notable negative for a runner ranked eighth of twenty-two.

runners_data.name: Blake's Monarch
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's runner has a form figure of 10th on latest start and was beaten at 6-2 last time; a 61-day absence and zero wins in three career starts on good ground make this an uphill task despite De Sousa in the saddle.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last three starts, Blake's Monarch does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a speed rating of 91 offers encouragement, though a 61-day absence and an unplaced effort last time out are the questions connections must answer from stall 16 off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Glorious Game
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly won her last two before a 9th place finish on latest; the headgear flag is notable, and Oisin Murphy's presence lifts the booking, but OR 88 and a concern about her latest run means she needs to bounce off that effort here.
runners_data.comment: Glorious Game won two of her last three starts, including a victory two runs back, and has run over today's trip, but she carries 128 lb from stall 10 and a struggling trainer — just one winner from 24 runners in the past fortnight — makes confidence hard to summon.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's juvenile is two wins from five on good ground and handles six furlongs well; Tom Marquand rides a horse that tracked the pace effectively to win last time — the natural style suits this chaotic race shape better than most in the prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after back-to-back wins, Innichen arrives on a 20-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going; carrying 128 lb from stall 3, his recent consistency is a plus, though that latest reverse is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: It Dunt Marra
runners_data.note: Won over five furlongs on good ground last time for Ollie Sangster; steps up to six furlongs for the first time here which is an unknown, and Stevie Donohoe needs to find cover in a 22-runner field — the trip question is real.
runners_data.comment: It Dunt Marra won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid each-way profile, but a rating of 86 and draw 20 leave him with plenty to do against a deep field of 22.

runners_data.name: Kodiak Breeze
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's two-time six-furlong winner on good ground has the pace profile to lead but competes for front rank with five stronger-rated horses; Shane Gray is a conditional booking in a hot race and OR 78 is below the class ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Kodiak Breeze arrives in fine nick — a winner two of his last three starts, including back-to-back victories — and has experience over today's trip and going, but a 50-day absence and a trainer firing at just 5% recently are real concerns at 128 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Toledo
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's OR 120 runner won over this exact trip on latest start and has the highest combined rating among the prominent types; Callum Rodriguez rides a horse whose form figures of 5-1 are misleading — the win was high-class and his profile suits a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but ranked 16 of 22 on our figures, with a speed rating of 65 suggesting that victory came in modest company; he has run over today's trip and the trainer is hitting a solid 27% strike rate, but it is hard to fancy him against stronger rivals from stall 21.

runners_data.name: Quillan
runners_data.note: Two wins from two starts, both on good ground over five furlongs, for David & Nicola Barron; Kaiya Fraser rides a horse stepping up to six furlongs for the first time — the stamina question is the only barrier to this being a live contender in a pace-dominated shape.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make Quillan the standout threat in the field, and he has experience of both today's trip and the going to complement that hot streak; the main query is whether 128 lb from stall 11 blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Satellite Of Love
runners_data.note: Clive Cox sends out a second string alongside Secret Society and Pride Of Toledo; Rossa Ryan on a horse that won both starts over six furlongs on good ground — the Cox yard's form is excellent (T14: 6/22) and this runner has a clean, uncluttered pace profile.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the rest on our figures despite winning his last two, Satellite Of Love arrives 33 days fresh and has run over today's trip, but a rating of 71 against a field of 22 makes him very hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Secret Society
runners_data.note: OR 120 and trained by Clive Cox but form figures of 6-3 suggest she has not won in two tries; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride but this horse is classified as a front-runner in a field saturated with pace — it may simply be outclassed at the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked 21 of 22 on our figures, Secret Society is hard to fancy despite the trainer's lively 27% strike rate; he has run over today's trip and was third last time out, but stall 18 and a speed rating of 52 make him a tough sell.

runners_data.name: Thebesthasyetocome
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's runner won over six furlongs on soft ground last time but only one run on good ground (3rd at five furlongs); 61 days off and a modest OR 83 mean this is a long-priced play in a race of this depth.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of these on our figures, Thebesthasyetocome faces a stiff ask at a rating of 74 in an 18-of-22 field, though he does return on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's second string has a 4-1-3 profile on good ground over six furlongs — solid consistency and James Doyle is a significant jockey upgrade; the horse tracks the pace naturally and the trainer's recent form (T14: 1/24) is modest, but Doyle's judgment could offset that.
runners_data.comment: Rated 12 lb below his official mark on our figures and ranked 17th of 22, Weekend Roar is hard to fancy, and a trainer striking at just 4% in the past fortnight adds little confidence; a winner two starts back and with experience of today's trip and going, he carries 128 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Niewiadoma
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's runner carries a worrying fade flag — form of 1-9-0-0 including 25th and 17th on her last two starts — and the blinkers may be a desperation measure; OR 78 and Gina Mangan's amateur claim cannot mask a horse that appears badly out of form.
runners_data.comment: Niewiadoma has won in recent starts but has finished unplaced in each of her last two outings, and with her trainer yet to score in 22 attempts over the past fortnight, confidence is hard to muster; experience over today's trip and going offers some small consolation.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's runner with Sean Levey has natural prominent intent but that form of 2-1-0-6 includes a 6th last time; true style is prominent but the race shape forces it back into a midfield role it doesn't naturally suit, which meaningfully reduces the chance of a performance matching its best.
runners_data.comment: Rollthedicebaby showed she can win, landing a victory three starts back and finishing second four starts back, but her last two outings have disappointed; she has run over today's distance and going, and returns after 19 days, carrying 123 lb from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Speed of Sound
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's juvenile won over six furlongs on good ground last time for Saffie Osborne, climbing from 3rd to 2nd to 1st — progressive form at OR 81 and a natural prominent style that suits a strong pace; the concern is whether 15 days between runs is a touch quick.
runners_data.comment: Speed of Sound arrives in fine nick after winning last time out, with a second and third also in her recent starts suggesting consistent form, and she has run over today's trip before; the 123 lb burden from stall 22 may test her, however.

runners_data.name: Vollering
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's OR 96 runner has a headgear flag and a patchy recent sequence (1-5-4-3-6-2); Pierre-Louis Jamin rides and the horse has shown ability but the recent form trend is wrong, and the soft-ground wins are not matched by convincing good-ground performances over six furlongs.
runners_data.comment: Vollering shaped well when runner-up last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while 123 lb from stall 1 keeps connections thinking; the concern is a trainer without a winner in 22 attempts across the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Sun Goddess, Secret Society, Satellite Of Love, Blake's Monarch, Glorious Game, Quillan, and Kodiak Breeze all want to lead in a 22-runner field over six furlongs at York, guaranteeing a fierce early battle for position and a genuinely strong gallop from the outset. The congestion through the first two furlongs will be severe, with nine runners seeking prominent positions and the inevitable traffic squeeze hitting hardest between two and three furlongs out as the field fans across York's wide straight. Horses forced to race keenly against their will or unable to find early rhythm will be compromised, while those with the class and adaptability to settle just off a blistering pace — rather than being sucked into the front-running scrap — will emerge with the strongest finishing kicks. This race shape decisively favours prominent-to-midfield runners with proven stamina for six furlongs on good ground and a high Racing Post Rating, as the strong pace will find out anything one-dimensional; Furturra, Battle Fever, and Rollthedicebaby are genuine prominent types who are unlikely to secure their natural position given the volume of front-runners, and of the confirmed pace setters, Sun Goddess and Satellite Of Love hold the clearest tactical edge in terms of class and course form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Class Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the confirmed front-runners set a genuine scorching gallop and the race becomes a true test of six-furlong stamina on good ground.
scenarios.body: The multiple pace-setters fight hard early, stretching the field and burning out the weaker speed types, leaving the classier, better-rated horses who settle just off the pace to pick up the pieces from two furlongs out. Prominent runners with high ORs and strong good-ground form — particularly those stepping up from five furlongs who have already proven stamina — are the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Sun Goddess or Satellite Of Love — breaks cleanly, secures a handy lead without burning too much petrol, and dictates a strong but controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: With rivals scrapping for prominent spots behind, the controlling front-runner gets a rhythm advantage and can quicken at the two-furlong pole before rivals have organised their challenges. Sun Goddess, with Ryan Moore in the saddle and five good-ground runs under her belt, has the class and course form to make this scenario hers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace war burns through the true leaders and a well-placed prominent runner sits a length or two off the heat before unleashing a sustained run in the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse able to track the pace from the inside of the prominent group, avoid the worst of the early hustle, and accelerate smoothly from two furlongs out will find this shape perfectly suited. Innichen, Tokaido, and Weekend Roar all have the tactical profile to exploit this scenario, with the Clive Cox yard's runners Satellite Of Love and Pride Of Toledo also equipped for this role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so intense that even prominent runners are spent entering the final furlong, creating a rare late opening for genuine hold-up types to come from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: Where Love Lives and Mind Those Steps are the truest hold-up runners in the field and would need the field to string out dramatically, leaving a clear racing line on the outside. Given that several of the supposed hold-up horses (Furturra, Battle Fever, Rollthedicebaby) are redistributed prominent types unlikely to be genuine closers, the pool of true finishers is shallow and this scenario carries low probability.

watchPoints.text: Sun Goddess and Satellite Of Love both break from Clive Cox and A P O'Brien's yards with clean pace profiles — if either leads uncontested in the first furlong, the other confirmed front-runners (Secret Society, Blake's Monarch) may be sucked into a speed duel that burns the whole front rank.

With nine runners seeking prominent positions in a 22-runner field, watch for severe traffic trouble two to three furlongs out as the field fans across York's straight — horses drawn wide have a path but those on the rail face being squeezed at the critical moment.

Furturra, Battle Fever, and Rollthedicebaby are all natural prominent racers who have been pushed into midfield on the pace map — if any of them attempt to force their way forward early, they will burn energy needlessly and arrive at the two-furlong marker compromised.

Quillan and Kodiak Breeze are unbeaten but have never run over six furlongs — both face a genuine stamina test in a race where the pace will make the trip as demanding as it gets, and either could drop out quickly if the extra furlong finds them out.
Monitor the Clive Cox yard closely: Secret Society, Satellite Of Love, and Pride Of Toledo all run for the same stable — jockey tactics may differ

races.name: Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Point Lynas
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with strong course and distance form over this trip on Good ground, though a career-high OR of 108 on a 7yo body is a stiff ask; Callum Rodriguez retains and the trainer's 14-day strike rate is solid.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and consistent enough in recent starts, Point Lynas arrives here 25 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going before, and a trainer firing at 38% in the last fortnight boosts his claims, even if he remains winless in his last five.

runners_data.name: Arctic Dawn
runners_data.note: Won on this going over 7f recently and steps up to a mile — the trip is a question mark given all five recent runs are over shorter; drops 12 days turnaround into a big field, likely to be covered up on the outside of the prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Arctic Dawn won last time out and has run over today's trip and conditions, giving him solid claims, but carrying 136 lb from stall one and ranking eleventh of seventeen on our rating suggests he faces a stiff ask against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Tudhope aboard for O'Meara, an excellent yard-jockey combination at York; sits prominently and has five of his last five runs on Good over a mile showing consistent placed form, making him a natural fit for the dominant pace shape here.
runners_data.comment: Cerulean Bay shaped well when second one start back and has run over today's trip and conditions before, giving him a solid platform from stall nine on a quick turnaround of twelve days; the worry is his latest ninth suggests he can run below that level.

runners_data.name: Centigrade
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — the key variable is whether the 63-day absence blunts his jump from the gate; handled artificial surfaces last two wins so the Good turf is a minor unknown, but Rossa Ryan will be instructed to roll and dictate.
runners_data.comment: Centigrade arrives on the back of two wins in his last three starts, including a victory last time out, but the 63-day absence is a concern and our rating ranks him near the foot of this field, making it hard to fancy despite his recent winning thread.

runners_data.name: The Lost King
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy in the saddle is a major upgrade angle — this horse has won over a mile on Good and recently ran well in similar-grade handicaps; prominent style is perfectly suited to sitting off Centigrade without getting sucked into the scrimmage for second slot.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving The Lost King solid claims, though a 40-day break and a patchy recent sequence — unplaced one start back — temper enthusiasm; he carries 132 lb from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Bullet Point
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a second over this trip on Good last time for Haggas; prominent style suits but the headgear note (previously worn) and a modest winning record at this level means he needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Bullet Point ran second last time out and returns quickly on 12 days' rest, having experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 108 suggesting he holds strong claims; the chief risk is a winless recent run of five starts.

runners_data.name: Checkandchallenge
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse dropping back from 10f; has placed at this trip and going combination before but winning form is absent at OR 99 over the mile; at 40 days off, likely to come from off the pace and needs a gap that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Checkandchallenge brings solid each-way claims after finishing third last time out, and his experience over today's trip and conditions is a genuine asset carrying 129 lb from stall six; the chief concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Blue Brother
runners_data.note: Ran second over this distance on Polytrack and placed over 7f Good; OR 98 and limited turf form over the mile make this an each-way proposition at best, and the 1/3 trainer strike rate in 14 days is thin sample evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Blue Brother at least shaped with a little promise when fourth one start back, though the eighth last time out is harder to spin; carrying 128 lb from stall five, he has run over today's trip and our rating of 108 offers some encouragement, but he needs to find improvement to force his way into contention.

runners_data.name: Eternal Force
runners_data.note: Won twice on soft ground and has a blinkers flag — softer conditions suit him better than today's Good; Browne McMonagle keeps the ride for Haggas but a 56-day absence and the going direction are mild concerns.
runners_data.comment: Eternal Force won back-to-back races earlier in this sequence but has since finished seventh and second in his last two starts, with a sixth last time out after a 56-day absence; he has run over today's trip and going, though that layoff and the stall-12 draw add a degree of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Mezcala
runners_data.note: Buick is always worth respecting in big-field handicaps — won over 7f and placed over a mile on Good, with genuine hold-up credentials making him one of the truest closers in the field; needs the congestion scenario to fire.
runners_data.comment: Mezcala showed his quality with a win one start back, but comes here on the back of an unplaced effort and faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 128 lb; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 105 suggests he holds some claims.

runners_data.name: Hawksbill
runners_data.note: Bottom of the weights at OR 93 and all five recent runs on Good over 7f — the step up to a mile on this course is untested, and modest form figures suggest he needs a collapse in the field above him to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Hawksbill has run over today's trip and going before but arrives winless in his last six starts, with a fifth one run back the closest he has come to threatening; carrying 123 lb from stall seven, he looks a midfield trader at best.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's sprinter-miler has won twice but recent form shows a persistent fade in the closing stages — his natural tendency is to push forward but in this field he is unlikely to secure a prominent position, meaning he races against his own instincts throughout.
runners_data.comment: Mirsky won in his last six starts but has posted three consecutive modest finishes since, and that string of nines and a seventh makes it hard to fancy him with confidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 123 lb from stall 16 rounds out a mixed profile.

runners_data.name: Nizam
runners_data.note: 63-day break at OR 92 and three recent runs show modest finishing positions; hold-up style and no wins on Good turf over seven or eight furlongs makes this a difficult proposition without significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well down our figures, Nizam is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after 63 days carrying 122 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Bethell's six-year-old placed recently at York over shorter — he wants to race prominently but with the glut of prominent types in this field, PJ McDonald is likely to find him shuffled into a midfield role that doesn't play to his strengths; trip is fine.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a second the start before, show Yorkshire in fair recent nick, though he remains winless in his last five starts; the trainer's 38% strike rate over the past fortnight is an encouraging angle, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Won twice over 7f on Good and placed at that trip recently — the step up to a mile is the key question; Ian Williams runs three horses in this race, which dilutes the yard's focus; hold-up style suits a congestion scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Aalto is hard to fancy at the weights, yet he does arrive on the back of a third last time out and a win the start before, and has run over today's trip and going before, offering at least some platform.

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard and placed over a mile on Good — a lightly raced four-year-old who naturally wants to race prominently, but the overcrowded pace positions mean Ray Dawson may be forced to drop him in; the style mismatch is a real setback.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Spell Master has been beaten into sixth and seventh in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy despite a third before that keeping some hope alive; distance and going experience and a 19-day turnaround offer little extra comfort.

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Another Ian Williams runner who is a true hold-up horse reassigned to a midfield position on the map; placed over 7f on Good last time, but without a win from 0W1P on similar going and a route that depends on traffic clearing, the chance is limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifteenth of seventeen on our figures, The Angel King faces a stiff ask here, though a second last time out at least shows he can threaten the places, and he has experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Centigrade is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to push him from the jump, he should control fractions on Good ground over York's straight mile — a setup that rewards those who can travel prominently behind him without expending early energy. However, this field contains a serious glut of prominent-minded horses: Point Lynas, Arctic Dawn, Cerulean Bay, The Lost King, Bullet Point, Blue Brother, and Eternal Force all want to sit in the first quarter of the field, meaning Centigrade will not be entirely alone up front and the prominent slots directly behind him will be fiercely contested in the opening two furlongs. Mirsky, Yorkshire, and Spell Master are genuine prominent types who will be squeezed into a midfield role against their natural instincts, creating a compressed, congested pack through the middle stages that raises traffic risk significantly from the two-furlong pole. The race shape strongly favours horses who can secure a clean, prominent position two or three lengths off Centigrade's shoulder without fighting for it — horses that find that slot naturally, travel smoothly, and carry momentum into the straight — rather than closers who will need to thread through a bunched field or front-runners who must overextend to hold a lead. With multiple prominent types redistributed out of role, the field is more truly prominent-biased than it appears on paper, and the runner who gets the ideal Position A off the pace without burning fuel will be hardest to peg back in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centigrade Controls, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Centigrade establishes a measured lead at a sensible gallop and the pace stays honest but not brutal, allowing a well-placed prominent horse to track and quicken.
scenarios.body: Centigrade sets a fair tempo under Rossa Ryan and is joined or passed inside the final furlong by a prominent traveller who has been coasting two to three lengths off the pace; the straight mile at York with Good ground rewards this profile — hold-up horses have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Centigrade and one bold prominent horse kick clear early and the congested midfield fails to organise a coherent challenge in time.
scenarios.body: With so many horses scrapping for position behind Centigrade, the immediate pursuers lose rhythm and the race effectively becomes a two-horse battle up front by the three-furlong pole; horses like The Lost King or Bullet Point, who travel prominently and quicken, benefit most if they secure the second slot cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congestion Frees Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster causes sustained interference from three furlongs out, creating a wall that splits or slows, allowing a hold-up horse to find a gap and sprint through.
scenarios.body: Mezcala or Checkandchallenge, sitting outside the scrum, finds a clean passage as the bunched prominent group checks slightly entering the final two furlongs; on Good ground York's wide straight can accommodate a late swoop if the gap appears early enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion among prominent types causes an uneven, stop-start pace that compresses the whole field into a sprint finish with no clear rail run.
scenarios.body: Redistribution of Mirsky, Yorkshire, and Spell Master into midfield roles means several horses race awkwardly and block routes; in a bunched finish, the horse with the clearest head of room and best finishing speed benefits — but this scenario is inherently unpredictable and depends on chaotic traffic resolving.

watchPoints.text: Centigrade (Rossa Ryan) must break cleanly from his stall — any missed break allows the prominent pack to swamp him immediately and negates his entire tactical advantage as lone pace-setter.

A seven-runner scramble for the three or four prominent slots directly behind Centigrade from the two-furlong mark to the halfway point creates a significant bump and interference risk — horses on the wide outside (Arctic Dawn, Blue Brother) may be least affected.

Mirsky, Yorkshire, and Spell Master are all natural prominent horses who will be reluctant passengers in midfield — watch for any of them pushing forward from the gate regardless of position, which could force an unexpectedly hot early pace and compromise Centigrade.

Mezcala (William Buick) will be held up and needs a clean split in the final two furlongs — in a 17-runner field on York's straight mile, watch where Buick positions him at halfway as an indicator of whether the closer scenario can materialise.

The Angel King, Aalto, and Nizam all represent Ian Williams with three runners — monitor market moves for any stable confidence signal, as one of the three may receive a tactical ride to suit the others.

races.name: Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Kalpana
runners_data.note: Five-year-old mare in fine form (four wins from last five, all at 12f on Good), Colin Keane aboard for a stable with a live 6/49 fortnight; headgear (hg:p) suggests she needs covering up and produces her best racing prominently just behind the pace — ideal race shape if honest gallop is set.
runners_data.comment: Kalpana arrives on the back of a win last time out, a placed effort two starts back sandwiched between victories, and has run over today's trip and going before — three wins in her last five starts make her the one to beat off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Minnie Hauk
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and A P O'Brien combination demands respect, and her sole win came over 10f on Good before being stretched to 12f at Group level; form figures at this trip are mixed but Moore's positional judgment gives her every chance if the pace collapses late.
runners_data.comment: Minnie Hauk catches the eye off a 26-day freshener, having run over today's distance and going before, and her second two starts back shows she retains the class to mix it at this level; the 135 lb burden is the one weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Tattycoram
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 12f Good-ground wins for Ralph Beckett make her the most in-form front-runner in the field; hg:p worn, 47 days since last run, and Edward Greatrex must deploy her forward from the off — if she dictates cleanly she is a serious threat.
runners_data.comment: Tattycoram won her last two starts encouragingly, though she ranks eighth of nine on our figures and a speed rating of 99 leaves plenty to prove against this company; the return after 47 days and experience of today's trip and going are the chief positives.

runners_data.name: Earth Shot
runners_data.note: William Haggas three-year-old with solid form at 10-12f on Good; shown at the rear of the map because the field is front-heavy and lighter on hold-up types, but her natural inclination is to race prominently — discount her if a true staying-on closer is required, though James Doyle can place her.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Earth Shot faces a stiff task on the back of a sixth last time out, and though she has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before, the overall profile makes her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old has a 2-3-1 run of form at 10-12f on Good and Oisin Murphy gives him a top-class pilot; trainer has 0/7 in the past fortnight which is worth noting, but the horse's improving profile and Good-ground record make him a legitimate each-way contender if the pace is strong.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a winner three starts back, Inis Mor brings solid recent form and distance-and-going experience to this, though her rating of 111 ranks her sixth of nine and 126 lb is no featherweight.

runners_data.name: Johanna Walsh
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's three-year-old wears a hood (hg:t) and has won over 12f on Good, with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle; as a confirmed front-runner she must lead or be very close, and the trainer's strong 6/59 fortnight reflects stable confidence.
runners_data.comment: Johanna Walsh arrives on the back of a win last time out, and her recent form reads with real consistency — two wins and three placings in her last five starts underline a filly in excellent nick. Carrying 126 lb is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Legacy Link
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden with William Buick is always a formidable combination, but 63 days since last run and a recent 7th on Good ground at 12f requires explanation; she has wins over 10f on Good and Buick will likely slot her just behind the lead battle rather than fight for the front.
runners_data.comment: Legacy Link showed smart form when winning three starts back and finishing second two starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going; the concern is a 63-day absence that leaves her fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: J S Bolger three-year-old with three wins from her last five and only 14 days since last run; races prominently and has won at 10-12f on Good, though 1m4f at York in a Group 1 is the stiffest test of her career and the trainer's 0/7 fortnight is a caution flag.
runners_data.comment: Sparan Nua won three of her last five starts and a third two starts back underlines her consistency, though she has not managed better than fourth latest and faces four rivals rated above her on our figures, with 126 lb to shoulder over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sugar Island
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's lower-rated runner (OR=102) has a modest recent form string (91-430) and her best win came over 8f on Heavy — the combination of a step up in class, 12f on Good ground, and no wins at this sort of level makes her the most exposed runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and without a win in her last three starts, Sugar Island faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and that sole recent win shows she can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Johanna Walsh, Tattycoram, and Legacy Link — plus Sugar Island (who has shown front-running tendencies at lower level) will contest the early lead in what promises to be a genuinely contested, honest gallop over 1m4f on Good ground at York. With prominent runners Kalpana, Minnie Hauk, Inis Mor, and Sparan Nua also wanting to sit close to the pace, there will be significant congestion in the first three furlongs as the field strings out around the long York straight; traffic danger is real 2-3 out for any horse caught in a pocket on the home turn. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their ideal position — Johanna Walsh (hg:t, strong recent form, Dylan Browne McMonagle) and Tattycoram (back-to-back wins, hg:p) are best-placed to actually dictate, with Legacy Link likely to slot in just behind after 63 days off. A genuine pace will stretch the field and test stamina thoroughly, meaning the race shape firmly favours horses who can travel prominently within the pace without over-committing, and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — the profile of a horse with an end-to-end gallop to run into, rather than one needing a false injection of speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Johanna Walsh and Tattycoram set a genuine, even pace and the field runs on in a line from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop removes the sprint finish and rewards horses travelling strongly in the first four, with the 1m4f York straight providing no hiding place for passengers; horses with proven Good-ground stamina at 12f+ take over late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Johanna Walsh or Tattycoram steals a decisive advantage from the front and the field is slow to react.
scenarios.body: One of the lead pair settles into an uncontested rhythm while rivals waste energy jostling for position behind them, and the long run-in at York means a well-rated front-runner with tactical freshness can hold on; Tattycoram's back-to-back wins and hg:p suggest confidence from the stable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the lead battle burns out the front three and a midfield mover produces a sustained challenge over the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Minnie Hauk (Ryan Moore, A P O'Brien) and Inis Mor are the most natural beneficiaries if the pace proves suicidal, swooping from just off the lead as the front-runners tie up; note however that Earth Shot, nominally shown at the rear, is a true prominent type redistributed there because the field is front-loaded, so its effectiveness as a genuine closer is overstated.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If early congestion causes chaos and the pace becomes ragged or briefly steadied before a sprint develops.
scenarios.body: A messy race with checks and shuffling would theoretically suit a hold-up horse producing a late burst, but the field contains no genuine deep hold-up specialist — Earth Shot is the closest profile and is racing out of role — making this the least likely and least well-populated scenario.

watchPoints.text: Johanna Walsh and Tattycoram are both confirmed front-runners drawn in a field with Legacy Link also wanting that ground — watch the first 3f for a genuine pace battle that could burn out all three and leave the race wide open at the 2f pole.

Kalpana wears headgear (hg:p) and is best covered up racing prominently — Colin Keane must find clean air on the outside or she risks being bottled in during the early positional scramble with four runners contesting the lead.

Legacy Link's 63-day absence is the longest in the field; Buick will likely slot her quietly behind the lead group, but if she is ring-rusty she may hang or find traffic at the critical turn for home, making her a place-first rather than win-first proposition.

Earth Shot is shown at the rear of the field map but is a natural prominent type redistributed there to balance a front-heavy field — do not interpret her position as a genuine hold-up role; she will likely race much closer to the pace than her mapped position suggests.

Sparan Nua's quick 14-day turnaround from her last run (4th) could be a fitness sharpener or a sign of trainer confidence, but at Group 1 level over a career-longest trip, watch whether she gets outpaced from the 3f mark if the gallop is truly honest.

races.name: British Ebf & Sir Henry Cecil Galtres Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ashariba
