runners_data.name: Club Class
runners_data.note: Six places from six tries on good or similar going is a model of consistency without winning; James Fanshawe in good 14-day form (6/24) and this 1m4f on good suits her travel-and-grind profile, but she needs a winner's instinct she hasn't yet shown.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent but frustrating, Club Class has finished second in each of her last three starts and is winless in recent starts, yet her experience over today's trip and going counts in her favour; the 135 lb burden is the obvious concern against sharper rivals.

runners_data.name: Merveilleux Lapin
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows filly (2/9 in 14 days) who holds solid form at 12f on good ground; her hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuine, which this race should provide, and Callum Rodriguez gives her a patient ride.|
runners_data.comment: Merveilleux Lapin has been placing consistently in recent starts, finishing third last time out and second three starts back, and she returns after 27 days in good heart with distance and going experience to call on; the main risk is she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Morrophore
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on a horse with three wins from four starts on good ground and a 215-day absence to overcome; John and Thady Gosden send him out fitter than that layoff suggests given their 4/16 strike rate, and his prominent style is ideally suited to this pace shape.|
runners_data.comment: Morrophore arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and boasts three victories in her last five starts, with experience of today's going adding further appeal; the concern is 215 days off the track, and she needs to bounce straight back to her best.

runners_data.name: Perfect Your Craft
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on good ground and showed in his last run (3rd at 14f, good) that the trip is within range; Pat Twomey's runner wears a hood and W J Lee rides, giving him a tactical edge in the prominent pack.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner five starts back, Perfect Your Craft arrives carrying 135 lb off a 43-day break having already shown she handles today's distance and going — the main concern is that absence.

runners_data.name: Rhapsody
runners_data.note: William Haggas in strong form (6/37 in 14 days) and Tom Marquand partners a mare who finished second at 10f on good ground last time; her hold-up style requires her to weave through traffic which is a real concern given the prominent congestion forecast.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner four starts back, Rhapsody has going experience in her favour but faces a stiff ask at 135 lb, and her fourth and third in between suggest inconsistency that could leave her vulnerable in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: Three wins at 10f-12f on good or soft for David O'Meara but hasn't run for 111 days; Tudhope takes the ride and the prominent style suits this shape, though the long absence and a recent sixth at 12f on good leaves a fitness question.|
runners_data.comment: Ryka hasn't run in 111 days and ranks twelfth of fifteen on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and solid experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: A La Prochaine
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo (8/33 T14) has placed twice at 12f in good-ground company and James Doyle's booking is always significant; only three career runs limits confidence but the form she has shown at this trip is encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Winner three starts back and third two starts back, A La Prochaine arrives on a 76-day break but has experience of today's trip and going, and her rating of 110 marks her as the one to beat in this field.

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo won at 8f on good and has placed at 10f; her natural tendency to race prominently is likely to be frustrated in a field with this many pace-seeking types, meaning she may find herself in a less comfortable position than her form requires.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Capichera faces a stiff ask off 126 lb, yet she does arrive in fair nick — third last time out, a winner two starts back — and has experience on today's going to draw on.

runners_data.name: K Sarra
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo wears a hood and has been declining since her debut win — 7th, 8th, 3rd and 11th in recent starts; Rossa Ryan partners but the form is heading the wrong direction and 12f on good has not brought out the best in her.|
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back and third three starts back show K Sarra has ability, but her last two outings — seventh and eighth — are hard to ignore; she has run over today's trip and going, and at 126 lb she faces a stiff task off a 97 official rating.

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's confirmed front-runner with Oisin Murphy aboard; won at 12f and placed three times, with course-form positives, and will push for the lead from the gate — the key question is whether he or Vauntingly controls the tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Prizeland has winning form in recent starts and ran second last time out, giving her a solid profile at 126 lb, though she sits ninth in the ratings among a competitive field and a fifth two starts back suggests vulnerability.

runners_data.name: Summerson
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly raced 3yo with an unknown preferred style (tagged U, hg:h); three runs all placed or won at 8-12f on good ground with Ray Dawson riding — the unknown quantity here, but the form quality is limited and Varian is 5/21 in 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of 15 on our figures and with a significant gap to her official rating of 96, Summerson is hard to fancy despite a lively recent sequence of a win last time out and seconds in her two prior starts, and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden's 3yo placed at 12f on good last time; she naturally wants to race prominently but the saturation of pace in this field makes that unlikely, and Billy Loughnane will need to adapt her ride accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Sunshine Star faces a stiff task against 14 rivals, though she has winning form in recent starts and a fourth last time out leaves her with plenty to find, even if she does bring distance and going experience to the table.

runners_data.name: Vauntingly
runners_data.note: The front-runner to watch — Dylan Browne McMonagle is aggressive from the gate, and Vauntingly's record of four placed efforts from five on good or similar ground at 10-12f shows consistency; the critical factor is whether he can manage the duel with Prizeland without burning out.|
runners_data.comment: Vauntingly arrives on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, and her recent record of a win and four placings in her last five starts shows consistent form, though she has been unable to build on her victory and the weight of 126 lb may not help her cause.

runners_data.name: Without Prejudice
runners_data.note: William Buick on a horse with a single run to his name — a 10f win on good ground for the Gosdens — making this only his second career outing; lightly raced horses with one run can be class animals or unexposed unknown quantities, and this one must prove he belongs at Listed level on a fraction of the experience of his rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well below most of her rivals on these figures, Without Prejudice faces a stiff task here, though she does arrive in form having won last time out twenty days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Vauntingly and Prizeland are confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, ensuring a genuine, honest gallop over this 1m4f on good ground — neither will yield cheaply, and with Oisin Murphy and Dylan Browne McMonagle both riding with intent, the early pace will be real rather than manufactured. Six of the fifteen runners are naturally prominent types, creating significant congestion between the lead and midfield from the two-furlong marker, with traffic dangers a serious concern for those caught in the pack at the bend. This pace shape — contested and honest but not suicidal — sets up the race most clearly for prominent-to-midfield types who can travel in range of the leaders without using their energy in early scrimmaging. Crucially, Sunshine Star and Capichera are genuine prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their natural position in this field given the volume of horses wanting that ground; Vauntingly and Prizeland are best placed to hold the front, with Club Class, Morrophore and Perfect Your Craft most likely to achieve true prominent berths behind them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Vauntingly and Prizeland drive each other along at a genuine clip and the race is decided by those who travelled smoothly just off that pace.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop stretches the field across the flat York straight, rewarding horses who covered the ground economically in the top half of the pack; this suits prominent racers who don't need to sprint from far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Soften, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace burns out the front-runners sufficiently to allow hold-up horses to pick them off in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Vauntingly and Prizeland both pay for their duel inside the final quarter-mile, opening a lane for horses held up with cover who have genuine finishing kicks; good ground suits horses with clean action coming late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Front Pair Slog
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop proves only moderate despite two front-runners, and one of the lead pair steals it with a controlled front-running display.
scenarios.body: Murphy on Prizeland or McMonagle on Vauntingly manages the pace rather than being forced into a duel, conserving enough to kick again inside the final furlong; prominent types that try to close find the leader has too much in reserve.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes significant interference two to three furlongs out and a horse given a creative wide route avoids trouble entirely.
scenarios.body: With six horses vying for prominent positions the field compacts dangerously entering the straight, leaving those given a clear outside run by an opportunistic jockey with a decisive advantage; Without Prejudice, lightly raced but clearly high-class, could exploit this with Buick's positional awareness.

watchPoints.text: Vauntingly and Prizeland will fight for the lead from the start — watch whether either concedes or if McMonagle and Murphy force a genuine duel that burns both horses out by the two-furlong marker.

The prominent congestion involving Club Class, Morrophore, Perfect Your Craft, Ryka and A La Prochaine creates a real traffic risk entering the straight — any horse caught pocketed on the rail two to three out faces a serious challenge finding daylight.

Morrophore returns from 215 days off for the Gosdens — watch the pre-race market move closely, as Ryan Moore's booking combined with that yard's current strike rate (4/16) suggests they are confident, but a fitness doubt remains live.

Without Prejudice is a massive unknown making only his second career start; William Buick's tactical intelligence could make him a live wide-runner in chaos, but the horse has zero experience of a field this competitive or a pace this demanding.

Sunshine Star and Capichera are both natural prominent types who may struggle to find their position in this field — watch where they end up in the early stages, as horses racing out of their comfort zone in the first half-mile at York rarely make up the lost ground.

races.name: Mews Hotel Ossett Ebf Stallions Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground recently and steps up in trip here for Richard Fahey; prominent style suits the shape but the 7f distance is an open question given his best form has come over shorter, and he has only 1 day since his last run which warrants scrutiny despite Fahey's recent form.
runners_data.comment: Boasting two wins in his last five starts, including a victory three starts back, Big Cigar has experience over today's trip and going and heads the ratings convincingly; the quick turnaround from just yesterday is the one query on an otherwise strong profile.

runners_data.name: Revels
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's consistent front-runner has won twice over 7f on Good ground and holds genuine claims to secure the lead; Sam James takes the ride and his record at the trip is strong, though he will face a fierce early battle from Perfect Nation and Weleyff for the front position.
runners_data.comment: Revels bounced back to winning form last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving connections every reason for optimism at 131 lb; the wide draw from stall 20 is the one factor to monitor.

runners_data.name: Shadow King
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's colt has a win over 6f Good ground and ran respectably over 7f at York last time; Sean Levey rides and the horse wears a hood, suggesting some temperament management is needed, though he is capable of travelling prominently and quickening.
runners_data.comment: Shadow King won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing consistent ability at this level, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the risk is that ninth last time out — a sharp drop in form he needs to put firmly behind him.

runners_data.name: Perfect Nation
runners_data.note: George Boughey's front-runner is in superb recent form with back-to-back wins including a 7f success on Standard, and Billy Loughnane is an excellent fit; will go hard for the lead against Revels and Weleyff, and the question is whether that early battle costs him late on.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Nation arrives on the back of two consecutive wins and a second in his last three starts, making him a compelling threat at 129 lb from stall four, though that weight could prove the critical test against a strong field.

runners_data.name: Soldier Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts over 6f Good ground for William Knight, stepping up in trip here for the first time; Hector Crouch takes the ride and the prominent style is suitable, though Knight's 14-day strike rate is modest and the trip beyond 6f is untested.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a win two starts back with a runner-up finish last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; rated 86 by both assessors, yet ranked 11th of 22 here, suggesting he faces stiffer opposition than recent form has tested.

runners_data.name: Weleyff
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's horse has won twice over 7f on Good ground and is arguably the most proven front-runner at the exact trip; Oisin Orr is a quality booking and Bethell's recent 14-day record is strong, making this a serious candidate to dictate from the front.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins heading into this, though he steps up in company here — ranked ninth of 22 on our figures — and 127 lb from stall 16 will test his resolve; the trainer's 38% strike rate over the past fortnight is a meaningful boost.

runners_data.name: Rising Tiger
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's consistent second-placer has been placed in all three starts over 7f on Good ground, carrying the prominent style well; Oisin Murphy's class is an asset but the lack of a win may reflect a tendency to be run out of it late when the gallop is truly strong.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts despite three runner-up finishes, Rising Tiger heads here ranked well down the field on our figures, and carrying 125 lb from stall 21 adds further complication; experience over today's trip and going is genuinely in his favour, but he remains frustratingly hard to place.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for David Evans who has struggled in recent races over 7f on Good, finishing fifth and eleventh in similar conditions; Saffie Osborne rides and the horse ran only 8 days ago, making freshness a question alongside a form profile that offers limited encouragement here.

runners_data.name: Bymiddaytomorrow
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's horse has won back-to-back over 7f on Good ground in excellent style, and Tom Marquand's booking underlines stable confidence; a prominent racing style means he should be able to settle into a good position without engaging in the early front-runner warfare.
runners_data.comment: Bymiddaytomorrow arrives on the back of consecutive wins and is fittingly fresh at just 13 days since her last run, with experience over today's trip and going also in her favour; however, her earlier finishes in recent starts show inconsistency, and a rating of 90 ranks her seventh of twenty-two here.

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 7f on Good ground recently for Ed Walker with Kieran Shoemark, and holds a win over 6f Good; the hold-up style means he is reliant on the pace being strong enough to create a gap late, which this race shape should provide in abundance.
runners_data.comment: Placed second in each of his last two starts, The Ginger Kid brings solid recent consistency to the table, and he has run over today's trip and going before; however, ranked eighth of twenty-two on our rating and carrying 124 lb from stall ten, he faces a stiff ask against the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: Mirzimaan
runners_data.note: William Buick's booking for this George Boughey hold-up runner immediately elevates interest; won over 6f Good and placed over 6f Standard, and steps up in trip to 7f where the strong pace should play to his late-running strengths on a course that rewards staying power.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner two starts back, Mirzimaan arrives on a 26-day break with experience of today's trip and going to his credit, though carrying 123 lb from stall 11 and ranked 12 of 22 on our rating suggests he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Telegraphic
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's prominent runner has won over 7f Good and placed twice at the trip, making his form highly course-and-distance relevant; Callum Shepherd has ridden him effectively and the horse's record of 1W2P in similar conditions is one of the most consistent profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Telegraphic won two starts back and ran second last time out, so fitness and form are both live; he has experience over today's trip and carries 123 lb from stall 14, though our rating of 84 leaves him with ground to make up on the principals.

runners_data.name: Caeruleus
runners_data.note: John Butler's hold-up runner has only one win on Tapeta and his sole Good-going start produced a fifth; David Egan takes the ride but the form in comparable conditions is thin and he is one of several rear-runners without the pace map position to express his natural style freely.
runners_data.comment: Caeruleus won two starts back and shaped with promise when third three starts back, but that fifth last time out tempers confidence; he has run over today's trip, returns on a reasonable 21-day break, and a trainer firing at 27% is a plus against a big field of 22.

runners_data.name: Mia Fantasia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's prominent runner won over 7f Good earlier this summer and Marco Ghiani rides; the form has tailed off since that win with a third and sixth in similar conditions, suggesting she may need things to fall perfectly her way to win off a mark that has risen.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back, Mia Fantasia brings fair claims with a distance experience and an 11-lb pull between official and our rating suggesting untapped potential; however, a below-par sixth last time out and a trainer firing at just 4% in recent weeks are real negatives to weigh.

runners_data.name: Roosike
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's runner won over 7f Standard and brings front-running tendencies that will add to the pace puzzle; Joe Leavy rides and while the horse is well-handicapped on that win, the step from Standard to Good ground is a genuine unknown and the early pace battle is brutal here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Roosike faces a stiff ask from stall eight off 120 lb, and while her recent form reads encouragingly — a winner last time out, second and third in the two starts prior — her speed rating of 69 leaves plenty to find on the 17-of-22 ranking.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's hold-up horse wears a hood and has a fine recent record of 1W3P over 5-7f on Good ground including a win last time; Aiden Brookes takes over and the form profile is better than the OR of 74 suggests, making this a potentially dangerous runner if traffic allows a run.
runners_data.comment: Koodini won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him obvious claims, but a struggling trainer — just one winner from twenty-four runners in the last fortnight — and a large field from stall twenty-two offer genuine reasons for caution.

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.note: Another Hugo Palmer hold-up runner wearing a hood, with form showing two places over 8f Good and a poor run over 7f last time; Cam Hardie rides but the last run saw him beaten into 16th over 7f on Good ground, which is a concerning recent data point for this trip and style.
runners_data.comment: High Hazard arrives on the back of an unplaced effort latest, though he showed promise with a third two starts back and a second three starts back; yet to win in recent starts, and a trainer striking at just 4% adds concern, though experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Regal Tiger
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's prominent runner has placed twice over 6f Good but never won; Andrew Mullen takes the ride and the horse is making a third start, but with no win on the board and three horses from the same stable competing, stable priorities may dilute the resources here.
runners_data.comment: Regal Tiger has shown consistency without converting, finishing second twice in his last three starts, yet he remains winless in that spell and ranks 18th of 22 on our figures, making it hard to fancy at these weights with a trainer firing at just 4% recently.

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's prominent runner won over 6f Firm and has placed over 7f Good, giving some encouragement at the trip; Silvestre De Sousa is a shrewd booking but the trainer's 14-day record of 1/4 is modest and the horse has not broken through at this level consistently.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Theheatison faces a stiff ask from stall 15 carrying 114 lb, and his speed rating of 68 gives little encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win in his last five starts at least shows he can find the front.

runners_data.name: High Calibre
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's hold-up runner has placed over 8f Good and holds a second from his most recent start; Sean Bowen takes the ride and while the step back to 7f from 8f may suit, the form on Good ground has not been strong enough to suggest he can win off a mark that demands improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, High Calibre faces a stiff ask from stall 18 carrying 114 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and was runner-up last time out.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner has shown a natural hold-up inclination across five runs on Good ground but has not won; Duran Fentiman rides and with the field's genuine hold-up types compressed toward the rear, this horse's OR of 70 and modest form profile make it difficult to see a winning route even if traffic clears — natural style is at the rear, not in midfield as mapped.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 19 of 22 on our figures, Rbflying makes a tough case to press, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a 21-day break carrying 114 lb from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner won over 6f Good last time and has shown a tendency to race towards the back; Tom Kiely-Marshall takes the amateur ride and 44 days off adds uncertainty, though the 7f trip on Good is a new question — genuinely a rear-runner by inclination, mapped forward here only because the hold-up positions are oversubscribed in this field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Fasthope is hard to fancy despite winning last time out, as two fifth-place finishes in the runs before that and a lowly speed rating of 64 tell against him, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Revels, Perfect Nation, and Weleyff are all confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field, and with Roosike also drawn and inclined to race prominently, this 7f York nursery will be run at a fierce, unrelenting gallop from the off — there is no scenario where the early pace is anything but strong. The three lead horses will jostle for rail position and shape through the first two furlongs, compressing the midfield and creating a wall of traffic 2-3 furlongs out where nine runners are competing for the same prominent berth. That sustained pressure over York's straight 7f on Good ground will stretch stamina reserves, turning the race into a test of resolution rather than a late burst, and the lack of any genuine false pace means the fractions will be honest throughout. This race shape strongly favours horses who can settle just off the pace in a genuine rhythm and produce a controlled, stamina-backed finish — true hold-up closers face a congested highway, while front-runners will be burnt by their own competition. Rbflying and Fasthope are genuine hold-up types but are mapped to midfield because the field holds more rear-runners than the pace map can accommodate at the back; of the front-runners, Revels and Weleyff look best placed to actually secure a prominent position given their recent winning form at the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed front-runners set a genuine end-to-end gallop and the race becomes a true test of 7f stamina on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Revels, Perfect Nation, and Weleyff burn each other off through the first half, and the race is won from just off the pace by a horse who settles beautifully and lengthens under pressure in the final two furlongs; Good ground at York rewards resolution over raw speed here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Surge
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner gains a decisive early break and the others fail to sustain, allowing a well-placed prominent runner to pounce from behind the lead.
scenarios.body: A clear leader briefly escapes the carnage of the early three-way battle, but a prominent stalker tracking slightly off the pace picks them up entering the final furlong with fresh legs; the horses who settled second or third in the pack without burning energy are best positioned.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion from furlongs 2-3 causes significant interference, bunching the midfield and leaving a clear run only to those held up furthest back.
scenarios.body: The squeeze through the pack frustrates the midfield cluster but opens a gap on the outside in the final furlong for a horse with genuine late acceleration; the hold-up horses who find daylight soonest will capitalise as tired front-runners fold.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three confirmed front-runners steals a march at the start, dictates an honest but not suicidal tempo, and holds every challenger safe.
scenarios.body: In a race with pace split three ways the lead horse who gets the cleanest break and settles into a rhythm rather than sprinting immediately has a slim chance of getting loose enough to be untracked; York's Good ground does not typically provide enough give to slow them, but a clear leader at the 3f pole is a genuine threat.

watchPoints.text: Revels, Perfect Nation, and Weleyff will collide for the lead in the first two furlongs — watch for one of them being checked or squeezed out in the scramble, which could fatally compromise any of their chances.

The prominent group of nine runners competing for the same real estate 2-3 furlongs out creates a serious traffic obstruction — watch the inside rail for horses being stopped in their run at the critical point entering the final two furlongs.

Mirzimaan's William Buick booking is the single most significant jockey upgrade in the race and should not be underestimated — watch where Buick positions him leaving the stalls, as any cover in midfield could turn into a decisive late burst.

Roosike adds a fourth possible front-runner to the mix and must be watched at the start — if she breaks well and gets a clean lead before the confirmed front-runners engage, she could complicate the tempo calculation entirely.

Koodini won last time and has form figures of 1-2-2-3 in recent runs, making the OR of 74 look lenient — watch whether Aiden Brookes can find a clear passage on the wide outside in the closing stages, which is the only route home for a genuine hold-up horse in this field.

races.name: British Ebf Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bellarchi
runners_data.note: Best recent form (three wins in last five) on Good ground at 7-8f, suited by a strong pace from hold-up position; Pierre-Louis Jamin rides and this trip on this going matches all her wins.|
runners_data.comment: Bellarchi has won four times in her last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs back, but a sixth last time out after 44 days off raises a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 140 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Royal Velvet
runners_data.note: Has won on Good ground at 7f on her last two starts, goes well fresh (22 days), but Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim must offset the 0/13 trainer 14-day strike and a wide draw in a 21-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Royal Velvet won back-to-back races four and five starts back, has experience of today's trip and going, and returns in decent order just 22 days on; the worry is that she has finished fifth in each of her last two starts, suggesting she may need to find more.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Andrew Balding and PJ McDonald; hasn't won at this trip and her form on Good has been modest, but she will set the pace and shape the race rather than win it.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mubasimah nonetheless rates highly on our figures and has run over today's trip and going before, making her a strong contender from stall 17; the risk is that recent form — unplaced last time out — offers little encouragement after a 62-day break.

runners_data.name: Lam Yai
runners_data.note: 299 days off the track is a serious query; showed pace over 5-6f on soft ground for Burke but stepping to 7f Good is an unknown, and the layoff means she cannot be trusted without evidence she retains condition.|
runners_data.comment: Lam Yai arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, while her official mark of 96 underlines her claims; the sole concern is 299 days off the track, which leaves fitness the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Angel
runners_data.note: Won twice at 8f on Good but last two runs have been 11th and 12th, and cheekpieces go on here; has ability at this level but out-of-form horses in big handicaps on their last two tries need to show why this differs.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts show Just Call Me Angel has ability, but back-to-back unplaced efforts since are a concern; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 127 lb from stall 16, and an official mark of 94 suggests she remains competitive if recapturing that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: Dual 7f Good-ground winner on her last two runs for Boughey; cheekpieces retained, Billy Loughnane has winning form with trainer, and a hold-up style suits this pace scenario perfectly — strong claims.|
runners_data.comment: Tryst won two of her last six starts, including back-to-back victories, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; however, her two efforts before that winning run were a sixth and seventh, suggesting some inconsistency, and 126 lb from stall 12 may not help.

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Two wins on Tapeta at Wolverhampton limit the Good-ground evidence; Oliver Stammers takes over in a 21-runner field, and Charlie Johnston's 5/34 in 14 days shows the yard in decent nick.|
runners_data.comment: Carnival Of Light arrives in fine nick, winning on each of her last two outings, though she carries 126 lb from stall 18 and her rating of 87 leaves her ranked towards the foot of this field — the recent winning momentum is the key asset to weigh against those negatives.

runners_data.name: Bella Lyra
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with placed form at this trip; Finley Marsh is a light claimer but 75 days off and artificial/soft ground form limits confidence she handles this pace on Good today.|
runners_data.comment: Bella Lyra has shown ability with two runner-up finishes in her recent starts, but a ninth and eighth in her last two runs are a concern, and 75 days off the track adds an unknown fitness angle; winless in her last five, she has plenty to prove from stall 19.

runners_data.name: Oolong Poobong
runners_data.note: Won over 7f Good for Bethell and travels tongue-tied; 64 days off the track and a step back from 8f but the trainer is in flying form (9/24), making her quietly interesting at a price.|
runners_data.comment: Oolong Poobong has experience over today's trip and conditions, and her trainer is firing at 38% in the past fortnight, but an unplaced run last time and a fifth before that are a concern and a 64-day absence adds a fitness question mark for this 125 lb assignment.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Hold-up type that has run consistently in the 4-7 range on Good ground at 6-7f for Katie Scott; rarely wins (746467 form) and Ray Dawson faces a tough task getting a clear run in a 21-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Figjam nonetheless catches the eye on our figures, rated 103 against an official mark of 90, and arrives here fit on just 12 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions to her credit.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse by style whose recent form is over 6f on Good; the field density means she cannot get her preferred closing position and will be shuffled into midfield, which is not where she wants to race over 7f.|
runners_data.comment: Beaujolais Nouveau won four starts back but has finished fourth, fourth and fifth in her last three, suggesting she needs things to fall right; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 23 days between runs keeps her fresh enough to go close if rediscovering that winning form.

runners_data.name: Caim
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Bethell and Tudhope who won over 8f soft and ran second over 7f soft; Good ground at 7f is untested and 86 days off means fitness is a question, though he will shape the early pace regardless.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Caim looks hard to fancy despite a win three starts back; she was beaten into fourth last time out and returns after an 86-day break, though the trainer is in cracking form and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes over on this Haggas-trained filly who has won twice on Good at 7f; a prominent-pressing style suits a race run at this tempo and she has the class and ground form to be competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Albaydaa won two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, but a fifth last time out and 57 days off the track are questions to answer, and she carries 122 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse that will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal in a 21-runner field; her seven-run form string shows no win at this level and she arrives having raced out of her natural role.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Perfect Part does at least bring experience over today's trip and going, and a second three starts back shows she can threaten at this level; a seventh last time out and 121 lb from stall eight are the checks.

runners_data.name: Machadadorp
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on a hat-trick horse for Balding who has won twice over 7f Good; will try to lead but faces several rivals for that role, and his tactical judgement gives this runner the best chance of surviving as a front-runner.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked a long way down the field on our figures, Machadadorp has questions to answer after finishing sixth last time out, and back-to-back wins three and four starts back feel increasingly distant; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 23 days between runs suggests she is fit enough to go.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.note: Three-race form string shows two wins and a second, all at 7-8f on Good or Soft for Gosden; will press for the lead and has the most progressive profile of the pace-setters, but a 21-runner handicap is a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Starlight Lass faces a stiff task despite a genuinely eye-catching recent run of two wins and a second in her last three starts; she has run over today's trip before, though 43 days off and a demanding 120 lb ask make her hard to fancy from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Starfinch
runners_data.note: Won over 6f and ran third over 7f on Good for Eustace; hold-up style means she relies on traffic clearing, and her form going (3/5 on Good) is limited compared to the main market protagonists.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Starfinch has looked inconsistent in recent starts — sixth and ninth before a third last time out — though she does bring distance and going experience and a win four starts back at least shows she can find the line.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: Has won at 6-7f on Good for Ed Walker and carries headgear as a hold-up type; Edward Greatrex rides and the 2W form at this level is solid, but she'll need pace to fall right in a large, competitive field.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Secret History faces a stiff ask from stall 14 carrying 116 lb, yet her recent form is genuinely eye-catching — third last time out, but a winner two starts back, and boasting three wins in her last five starts, with experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: Has been placed four times at 6f on Good without winning for Fahey; her form suggests she finishes in the places but struggles to convert, and stepping up to 7f in a 21-runner handicap raises the bar further.|
runners_data.comment: Cotai Belle has been a model of consistency, finishing second in four of her last five starts, yet that winning breakthrough continues to elude her — winless in recent starts, she remains frustratingly stuck at the silver medal position. Has run over today's trip and going, and returns after 29 days fresh enough to go again.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly who has run second five times in her last six, all on Good going; the field size will push her into a midfield role that is not her natural territory, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim has to be managed carefully.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Woohoo faces a stiff ask here despite five consecutive runner-up finishes suggesting she is consistent if frustrating, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Zooella
runners_data.note: Won twice over 6f for Ralph Beckett and will attempt to lead at 7f; Good ground at this trip is slightly untested (1/6 in similar going) and she'll need to find a position in a multi-front-runner scramble.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 19 of 21 on our figures, Zooella faces a stiff ask off 114 lb from stall 11, and a speed rating of 64 leaves her well short of what is likely needed here, despite back-to-back wins in her last two starts and experience over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Mubasimah, Caim, Machadadorp, Starlight Lass, and Zooella all carry genuine front-running or pace-pressing profiles, meaning this 7f York contest will be run at a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset with multiple horses competing for the lead across a wide draw. York's flat 7f strip is unforgiving in big-field handicaps when the pace is genuine — leaders tend to empty in the final furlong, rewarding horses who travel in midfield or just off the pace and have a true staying kick. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically sit at the rear of a 21-runner field; Beaujolais Nouveau, Perfect Part, and Woohoo are genuine closers that will be pushed forward into midfield roles by race traffic and field density, meaning they will not be racing in their natural element. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with 7f stamina on Good ground — horses who can sit just behind the contested early fractions and deliver a sustained late run, rather than those who need either a clear lead or a true closing position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfielders Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace among Mubasimah, Caim, Machadadorp, Starlight Lass and Zooella ensures a genuinely strong gallop and the leaders have nothing left entering the final 2f.
scenarios.body: The front-runners will have burned each other out by the 2f pole, leaving the race to those who tracked the pace in midfield and have a proper 7f stamina profile; York's flat finish then rewards the horse who runs through on the bridle rather than having to sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-pressing horses settles just off the contested lead, conserves energy in the first half, and kicks clear when the true front-runners crack.
scenarios.body: A horse like Albaydaa or Carnival Of Light, sitting one or two lengths off the early scrimmage, would find their rivals empty around them and hit the line running; the contested pace does the damage for them without ever having to fight for the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the named pace horses — most likely Machadadorp or Starlight Lass — settles marginally better than rivals and dictates from a position just off the very sharp end before pressing on.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners and potential for traffic issues to slow the pursuit, a single front-runner who escapes the early battle and is allowed to dictate solo could build an unassailable advantage; Oisin Murphy's tactical awareness on Machadadorp makes this the most plausible single-lead survivor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fastest
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace, though genuine, does not fully unwind the field and genuine hold-up horses find sufficient daylight to deliver a late surge from behind midfield.
scenarios.body: This shape is discounted because Beaujolais Nouveau, Perfect Part, and Woohoo — the natural closers — are all redistributed to midfield by race traffic and will not enjoy their preferred closing position; the probability of a true hold-up winner is therefore materially reduced.

watchPoints.text: Machadadorp, Mubasimah, Caim, Starlight Lass and Zooella all want to lead — watch the first furlong closely for a fierce pace battle that could compromise all of them before the race truly begins.

Tryst has won her last two starts over 7f Good and arrives in the hold-up position that best suits this contested-pace scenario — if she travels smoothly through the field, she is the one to follow turning in.

Bellarchi and Royal Velvet are both genuine hold-up types who have shown the ability to win on Good ground at this trip; in a 21-runner field, their chances hinge entirely on finding a clean passage in the final 2f.

Woohoo, Beaujolais Nouveau and Perfect Part are true closers forced into midfield by field size — watch whether they are outpaced early or can gradually work through, as neither outcome is guaranteed and the style mismatch is material.

Oolong Poobong is quietly interesting for Bethell (trainer in form at 9/24 in 14 days) returning from 64 days off; watch for her to be produced with a well-timed challenge around the 2f pole if she has come back ready.
